_about: This file IS the ICP scoring model. It is data, not code, on purpose: a sales or RevOps leader should be able to read this file, disagree with a number, change it, and re-run the demo without touching Python. Every weight below is illustrative for a generic B2B seller of a mid-market software product and should be replaced with your own definition of a good customer.

fit_model._comment: Fit = static, slow-changing signals: who this company IS. Never mix with intent below.

intent_model._comment: Intent = dynamic, time-decaying signals: is something happening RIGHT NOW that makes this a good moment to reach out. Recomputed on every scoring run, never cached like fit.

recency_decay._comment: A signal loses half its value every half_life_days. A 6-month-old 'funding round' is background noise, not timing.

tiering._comment: Thresholds are calibrated against the synthetic universe in synth.py so that fit tiers roughly follow a 25/55/20 (A/B/C) split and intent tiers roughly follow a 10/25/65 (1/2/3) split. Recalibrate against your own data, these are not universal constants.

tier_notes.A1: Best-fit account, active buying signal now. Call today.
tier_notes.A2: Best-fit account, moderate signal. Nurture into a trigger event.
tier_notes.A3: Best-fit account, no signal. Long-cycle nurture, not a cold call target.
tier_notes.B1: Workable fit, strong timing. Worth a call despite imperfect fit.
tier_notes.B2: Workable fit, moderate timing. Standard pipeline.
tier_notes.B3: Workable fit, no timing. Low priority, marketing-only.
tier_notes.C1: Poor fit, active signal. Usually noise (wrong-size company reacting to something unrelated); verify before calling.
tier_notes.C3: Poor fit, no signal. Suppress from active lists.

contactability_model._comment: Whether the record is actually actionable, independent of how good the account is. A perfect A1 you cannot reach is worth zero this quarter.
contactability_model._shared_phone_threshold_comment: A phone number seen on this many or more distinct companies is treated as a shared line (accountant, registered-office agent, or call centre), not a direct company line.
